title: Run every repo gate green against the migrated tree
description:
Gate by gate, with what a failure in each actually means:

  pnpm test:sherif  - dependency version consistency across packages/*. A failure
                      means A4 (the packages/store bench bump) did not land, leaving
                      two solid-js versions. Baseline: green today.
  pnpm test:knip    - unused deps/exports. @solidjs/web may need an ignoreDependencies
                      entry for packages/solid-store if knip cannot see it through the
                      plugin config. packages/vue-store is the precedent.
  pnpm test:eslint  - includes the new braced-effect-half rule from A5.
  pnpm test:lib     - the semantic gate. A value one update behind means a missing
                      settle(); a REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE throw means ownedWrite
                      was dropped; REACTIVITY_HALTED means an effect half returned a
                      non-function.
  pnpm test:types   - runs TS 5.6, 5.7, 5.8 and 6.0. Verified clean during planning
                      against a representative probe, so a failure here is a real
                      signature problem rather than a toolchain surprise.
  pnpm build        - tsdown + tsc -p tsconfig.source.json
  pnpm test:build   - publint --strict
  pnpm test:docs    - scripts/verify-links.ts

Then pnpm test:ci for the whole thing.
acceptance_criteria: all of the following pass from the repo root: pnpm test:sherif, test:knip, test:eslint, test:lib, test:types, build, test:build, test:docs - i.e. pnpm test:ci is green.
close_reason: Full gate run green. pnpm test:ci: 'Successfully ran targets test:sherif, test:knip, test:eslint, test:lib, test:types, test:build, build for 46 projects'. test:types covers TS 5.6/5.7/5.8/6.0. solid-store suite: 46 tests across 4 files, no type errors. verify-links clean (needs Node 24 per .nvmrc; Node 22 cannot run the .ts script).

title: Add Solid 2 semantic contract suite
description:
New file, e.g. packages/solid-store/tests/solid2-semantics.test.tsx.

Contracts to pin:

(a) ownedWrite regression
    Render a component whose body calls useSelector, then fire the external producer
    (store.setState) from a context that inherits an owned scope. Assert no throw.
    Without ownedWrite: true this is REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE.

(b) coalescing
    N writes in one synchronous tick, one settle() => the selector observes one
    update, not N.

(c) consecutive functional updates
    store.setState(p => p + 1); store.setState(p => p + 1) with no settle between
    lands on +2. (Solid 2's functional setter prev IS pending-aware, even though
    reads are not - that asymmetry is worth pinning.)

(d) stale-window pin
    store.setState(1); expect(selected()).toBe(0)  // explicitly stale
    settle();          expect(selected()).toBe(1)

(e) microtask auto-settle
    store.setState(1); await Promise.resolve(); expect(selected()).toBe(1)
    with no explicit flush. The staleness window is exactly the synchronous tick of
    the write - the write itself arms queueMicrotask(flush).

(f) settleOnRead opt-in
    const s = useSelector(store, sel, { settleOnRead: true })
    store.setState(1); expect(s()).toBe(1)   // no settle() call
    This test must never gain a settle() between the write and the read.

(g) subscribe/unsubscribe contract
    - after disposing the owning root, a subsequent setState does not write
    - double dispose does not throw
    - the store has no dangling listener after disposal
design: These are the tests that would have caught real bugs in the reference migration. Types catch none of them. || (a) is the ownedWrite regression - construct useSelector inside a component body, trigger the external producer, assert no throw. || (d) is the one people push back on: asserting staleness looks like asserting a bug. It is the opposite - it turns the deferral from an accident into a documented contract, so a future change that silently makes reads synchronous again is caught. || (g) matters because Solid 2 nested roots are parent-owned, making double-dispose reachable; the reference implementation confirms late and double dispose never throw, so no extra guarding is needed - but assert it rather than assume it.
acceptance_criteria: a new test file pins, at minimum: (a) a write from inside a component body does not throw; (b) N writes in one tick coalesce; (c) consecutive functional updates see each other; (d) an imperative same-tick read is explicitly asserted STALE; (e) one awaited microtask settles without an explicit flush; (f) settleOnRead: true gives read-your-writes with no flush; (g) unsubscribe-on-dispose, including that a post-disposal setState writes nothing and double dispose is safe.

title: Migrate tests/index.test.tsx to Solid 2 timing
description:
packages/solid-store/tests/index.test.tsx is 363 lines and currently assumes
synchronous read-after-write throughout. Every one of these needs a settle():

  - 'useSelector reads mutable atom state and updates when changed'   (~line 20)
  - 'useAtom returns the current accessor and setter'                  (~line 31)
  - 'useSelector reads writable and readonly store state'              (~line 62)
  - 'useSelector only updates the accessor when selected state changes'(~lines 84, 90)
  - 'useSelector respects custom compare'                              (~lines 123, 131)
  - 'useSelector works with mounted derived stores'                    (~line 150)
  - useStore alias tests x2                                            (~lines 163, 174)
  - _useStore tests x2                                                 (~lines 192, 204)
  - createStoreContext 'provides bundled writable atoms and stores'    (~lines 241-245)

The createStoreContext one is the most interesting: it asserts the DOM synchronously
after an external .set(), so it needs settle() before getByText.

Pattern:
  atom.set((prev) => prev + 1)
  settle()
  expect(result()).toBe(1)

Do NOT reach for settleOnRead here to avoid the churn. The whole point of decision 3
is that deferred is the default and the tests demonstrate the real contract.

The shallow() describe block (lines 262-363) is pure function testing with no Solid
involvement - leave it entirely alone.
design: The renderSpy assertions (expect(renderSpy).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1) at lines 82/88/95 and 121/129/138) assert that Solid never re-runs the component body - a fine-grained guarantee that should still hold under Solid 2. If one of them fails, that is a real finding about the port, not a test to relax. Investigate before touching it. || Keep the explicit afterEach(cleanup) in tests/test-setup.ts: @solidjs/testing-library's auto-cleanup only engages when a global afterEach exists, and this project's vitest config does not set globals.
acceptance_criteria: every store mutation followed by an assertion has an intervening settle(); the createStoreContext DOM assertions pass; the renderSpy 'called once' assertions still hold unchanged; pnpm --filter @tanstack/solid-store test:lib is green.

title: Add the Solid 2 test harness (settle helper)
description:
Create packages/solid-store/tests/utils/reactive.ts:

  import { createRoot, flush } from 'solid-js'

  /**
   * Drains the Solid 2 reactive queue.
   *
   * Solid 2 defers every update to a microtask, so a test that reads a selector
   * imperatively after a store write must settle first. Idempotent and ~free when
   * the queue is empty (measured at ~11ns/op in the reference implementation).
   *
   * MUST NOT be called from inside onSettled or createTrackedEffect callbacks -
   * flush() is not reentrant there and throws.
   */
  export function settle(): void {
    flush()
  }

  /**
   * Runs `setup` inside a disposable root and hands back both the root's value and
   * its dispose. Writes to plain signals created in `setup` must happen AFTER this
   * returns - Solid 2 hard-throws REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE for writes inside
   * owned scopes unless the signal opted into ownedWrite.
   */
  export function createEffectTestRoot<T>(setup: () => T): {
    dispose: () => void
    value: T
  } { ... }
design: Model on table/packages/solid-table/tests/utils/reactive.ts. Deliberately a thin wrapper rather than a clever helper: the value is that every settle point in the suite is greppable and named, so the timing contract is visible in the tests instead of hidden behind an await. A settleAsync() variant existed briefly in the table repo and was dropped as unused - prefer the inline 'flush(); await Promise.resolve(); flush()' when a test genuinely needs to cross a microtask.
acceptance_criteria: packages/solid-store/tests/utils/reactive.ts exports settle() wrapping flush() from solid-js, plus a createEffectTestRoot helper; its doc comment states that settle() must never be called from inside onSettled or createTrackedEffect.

title: Port createStoreContext.tsx to Solid 2 context-as-provider
description:
Edit packages/solid-store/src/createStoreContext.tsx. Three mechanical changes:

  - import type { JSX, ParentProps } from 'solid-js'
  + import type { ParentProps } from 'solid-js'
  + import type { JSX } from '@solidjs/web'

  -   const Context = createContext<TValue>()
  +   const Context = createContext<TValue | null>(null)

  -     return <Context.Provider value={props.value}>{props.children}</Context.Provider>
  +     return <Context value={props.value}>{props.children}</Context>

  -     if (value === undefined) {
  +     if (value === null) {
          throw new Error('Missing StoreProvider for StoreContext')

ParentProps is still exported from solid-js (via ./client/component.js). JSX is not -
its namespace now lives in @solidjs/web/types/jsx.d.ts.

Alternative considered and not taken: typing the return as Element from solid-js
instead of JSX.Element. It avoids the @solidjs/web type import but shadows the global
DOM Element type, which reads worse. @solidjs/web is a peer either way.

This file is also the reason the built dist imports @solidjs/web at all - the JSX
compiles to createComponent(Context, ...). See the SSR-safety issue in the gates epic.
design: Keeping an explicit null default rather than Solid 2's default-less createContext<T>() is deliberate. Solid 2's JSDoc now recommends the default-less form because useContext then throws ContextNotFoundError and the return type is T with no narrowing. We decline that here because it would silently replace this package's documented public contract - the @throws tag on createStoreContext promises a specific actionable message, and the existing test asserts that exact string. || The throw must stay in the component BODY. A throw from inside a JSX expression triggers REACTIVITY_HALTED and kills every later render, turning an actionable error into a dead app. It already is in the body; just do not move it. || Solid 2's Context<T> extends ContextProviderComponent<T>, i.e. the context object IS the provider component, so <Context.Provider> no longer exists.
acceptance_criteria: JSX type is imported from @solidjs/web and ParentProps still from solid-js; the context is created as createContext<TValue | null>(null); the provider renders <Context value={...}> with no .Provider; the missing-provider check tests for null and still throws 'Missing StoreProvider for StoreContext' from the component body.

title: Rewrite useSelector.ts for Solid 2
design: ownedWrite: true is mandatory, not optional hygiene. @tanstack/store notifies subscribers synchronously from atom.set (propagate -> shallowPropagate -> flush, packages/store/src/atom.ts:249-261), and we do not control where set() is called from - if it fires during a component's setup or inside an effect, our setSignal write inherits that owned scope and throws REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE in dev. || Both halves of the settle guard are load-bearing. Flushing whenever there is merely no observer drains the pending queue into a MOUNTING component's owned scope and crashes; this was a real crash in the table adapter, fixed by adding the owner half (commit 0ae33c469). || The cast is required and its placement is exact, verified with tsc: createSignal overload 1 is (value: Exclude<T, Function>, options?) => Signal<T>, so the initial value needs 'as Exclude<TSelected, Function>' or it is a hard TS2769; the functional setter call setSignal(() => selector(snapshot)) needs NO cast. || No Observer-object normalization is needed: Store.subscribe and ReadonlyStore.subscribe already funnel through toObserver() internally, and atom.subscribe swallows its own first emission via the observed.current guard, so a bare callback is correct and the eager-emission/dedup dance the table repo needed does not apply.
acceptance_criteria: the signal is created with ownedWrite: true, name: 'store/useSelector' and equals: compare; the initial value is cast as Exclude<TSelected, Function>; UseSelectorOptions gains an optional settleOnRead documented as off by default; when settleOnRead is set, the returned accessor flushes only when getObserver() and getOwner() are BOTH null; a write from inside a component body does not throw.

title: Install, reconcile lockfile, and confirm workspace hygiene gates
description:
node_modules is NOT currently installed in this repo, so this is also the first real
install of the migration.

Steps:

2. Inspect the peer warnings. An unmet @solidjs/testing-library peer means the A2

   in package.json (pnpm 11 ignores the latter).
3. grep -rn '"solid-js"' --include=package.json packages examples
   Every hit should read 2.0.0-beta.30.
4. pnpm test:sherif   (baseline: it reports "No issues found" today - keep it there)

title: Move packages/store Solid benchmark to Solid 2
description:
packages/store/tests/derived.bench.ts:4 imports createEffect, createMemo and
createSignal from solid-js for a comparative benchmark (bench('Solid', ...), lines
62-76). It is the sole consumer of packages/store's solid-js devDependency.

Two changes:
1. packages/store/package.json: solid-js ^1.9.12 -> 2.0.0-beta.30
2. tests/derived.bench.ts: the one-arg createEffect(fn) form is removed in Solid 2 and
   types as never. Convert to the two-arg form:

     createEffect(
       () => source(),        // tracked compute half
       (v) => { sink(v) },    // untracked effect half - MUST be a braced block
     )

CRITICAL: the effect half must be a braced block. It may return a cleanup function;
if it returns anything else that is not a function, ALL reactivity in the process
permanently halts (REACTIVITY_HALTED) and it is silent. An expression-bodied arrow
leaks its expression value into the cleanup slot, which is exactly how this happens.

Also check whether the bench needs vite/vitest resolve conditions, since
packages/store's vitest setup does NOT run vite-plugin-solid and solid-js@2 maps the
bare node condition to an inert server build where effects never run. If so, add:

  resolve: { conditions: ['browser', 'development'] },
  ssr: { resolve: { conditions: ['browser', 'development'] } },
  test: { server: { deps: { inline: [/solid-js/] } } }
design: This is the only Solid touchpoint outside packages/solid-store and examples/. It matters because sherif enforces consistent dependency versions across packages/* (examples are exempt via the ignorePackage config in root package.json, but packages/store is not). Leaving it on ^1.9.12 while solid-store moves to 2.0.0-beta.30 breaks test:sherif. The table repo worked around the equivalent problem with sherif --ignore-dependency solid-js; migrating the bench instead keeps exactly one solid-js version and avoids the ignore.
acceptance_criteria: packages/store/package.json devDependency solid-js is 2.0.0-beta.30; tests/derived.bench.ts uses the two-arg createEffect with a braced effect half and runs; pnpm test:sherif reports no version mismatch for solid-js.

title: Flip jsxImportSource to @solidjs/web across all four solid-store tsconfigs
design: Missing the flip is a hard TS2875 (positive control confirmed in the table repo's spike). customConditions is needed because solid-js@2 maps the bare node condition to dist/server.js, an inert server runtime - typecheck must resolve the same browser/development build that vite-plugin-solid selects at runtime. customConditions requires moduleResolution node16/nodenext/bundler; the root tsconfig already sets Bundler.
acceptance_criteria: tsconfig.json, tsconfig.build.json, tsconfig.source.json and tsconfig.docs.json all resolve to jsxImportSource=@solidjs/web; tsconfig.json additionally sets customConditions [browser, development]; tsc -p each config emits no TS2875.

title: Relax @solidjs/testing-library peer ranges via pnpm-workspace packageExtensions
description:
@solidjs/testing-library@1.0.0-beta.2 declares peerDependencies of solid-js >=2.0.0 and
@solidjs/web >=2.0.0. Under semver prerelease rules neither matches 2.0.0-beta.30, so
pnpm reports unmet peers. Relax them.

Add to pnpm-workspace.yaml:

  packageExtensions:
    # Solid 2 transition (remove at Solid 2 GA): testing-library's >=2.0.0 peers do
    # not match 2.0.0-beta.x prereleases.
    '@solidjs/testing-library':
      peerDependencies:
        solid-js: '>=2.0.0-0 <3.0.0'
        '@solidjs/web': '>=2.0.0-0 <3.0.0'

NOTE: unlike the table repo, we do NOT need a vite-plugin-solid extension for
@testing-library/jest-dom. vite-plugin-solid@3.0.0-next.21 peers jest-dom at
^5.16.6 || ^5.17.0 || ^6.*, and this repo is on ^6.9.1 - already in range. The table
repo needed it only because it was on jest-dom 7.
design: It MUST go in pnpm-workspace.yaml, not package.json: pnpm 11 ignores the pnpm.packageExtensions field in package.json entirely. This repo is on pnpm@11.1.0 and already has an inert pnpm.packageExtensions block in root package.json for @vue/composition-api - do not follow that example. (Table repo bead table-sc8.4 learned this the hard way.)
acceptance_criteria: pnpm-workspace.yaml contains a packageExtensions block relaxing @solidjs/testing-library's solid-js and @solidjs/web peers to >=2.0.0-0 <3.0.0, with a comment marking it removable at Solid 2 GA; pnpm install reports no unmet peer for @solidjs/testing-library.
notes:
CORRECTION to the plan: packageExtensions does NOT work for this. pnpm merges packageExtensions into a manifest but does not override a peerDependencies key that already exists, so @solidjs/testing-library's declared '>=2.0.0' survived and the unmet-peer warning persisted through a full re-resolve.

The working mechanism is peerDependencyRules.allowedVersions, which is also this repo's existing idiom (it already carries '@vue/composition-api>vue'). Landed as:

  peerDependencyRules:
    allowedVersions:
      '@solidjs/testing-library>solid-js': '>=2.0.0-0 <3.0.0'
      '@solidjs/testing-library>@solidjs/web': '>=2.0.0-0 <3.0.0'

Verified: pnpm peers check reports zero solid-related issues after this.

Separately noticed: root package.json still carries a pnpm.packageExtensions block for @vue/composition-api that pnpm 11 prints a WARN about on every install and ignores entirely. Pre-existing dead config, harmless, not touched here.

title: Repoint @tanstack/solid-store dependencies at Solid 2 beta.30
description:
Edit packages/solid-store/package.json.

Current state:
  peerDependencies: { "solid-js": "^1.6.0" }
  devDependencies:  { "@solidjs/testing-library": "^0.8.10", "solid-js": "^1.9.12",
                      "vite-plugin-solid": "^2.11.12" }

Target state:
  peerDependencies: { "solid-js": ">=2.0.0-beta.30 <3.0.0",
                      "@solidjs/web": ">=2.0.0-beta.30 <3.0.0" }
  devDependencies:  { "@solidjs/testing-library": "1.0.0-beta.2",
                      "@solidjs/web": "2.0.0-beta.30",
                      "solid-js": "2.0.0-beta.30",
                      "vite-plugin-solid": "3.0.0-next.21" }

Verified compatible: vite-plugin-solid@3.0.0-next.21 peers solid-js and @solidjs/web at
>=2.0.0-beta.29 <2.0.0-experimental.0, which beta.30 satisfies. @solidjs/web@2.0.0-beta.30
peers solid-js at ^2.0.0-beta.30.
design: Range form is load-bearing: a bare >=2.0.0 does NOT match 2.0.0-beta.30, because semver only admits a prerelease when some comparator in the range shares its [major,minor,patch] tuple. >=2.0.0-beta.30 <3.0.0 does match. @solidjs/web must be a peer rather than a dependency - @tanstack/solid-router ships it as a regular dep and that is a bug to not copy, because it risks two copies of the web runtime in one graph. Dev deps are pinned exact because @solidjs/web peer-pins solid-js to the same beta; they bump in lockstep and must never be bumped singly.
acceptance_criteria: peerDependencies list solid-js and @solidjs/web at >=2.0.0-beta.30 <3.0.0; devDependencies pin solid-js and @solidjs/web to exactly 2.0.0-beta.30, @solidjs/testing-library to 1.0.0-beta.2 and vite-plugin-solid to 3.0.0-next.21; @solidjs/web appears in peerDependencies and devDependencies but NOT in dependencies.

title: Solid 2 adapter source port
description:
Port the ~180 lines of Solid binding in packages/solid-store/src to Solid 2.

Almost none of this is logic. The framework-agnostic @tanstack/store core works under
Solid 2 untouched; what changes is reactivity glue. Only two files carry real change:
useSelector.ts (the signal bridge) and createStoreContext.tsx (context-as-provider).
useAtom.ts, useStore.ts and _useStore.ts import only the Accessor type, which still
lives in solid-js, and are expected to need nothing.

The two Solid 2 behaviours that bite here:
1. Writing a plain signal from inside an owned reactive scope is a dev-time throw
   (REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE). We do not control where @tanstack/store's set()
   is called from, so the subscription callback inherits whatever scope the producer
   was in. The escape is the ownedWrite: true signal option.
2. Every update settles on a microtask, so an imperative read in the same synchronous
   tick returns the previous value. Handled by the settleOnRead opt-in (see the tests
   epic for how that becomes a pinned contract).
acceptance_criteria: packages/solid-store/src compiles clean under tsc with jsxImportSource=@solidjs/web; no imports remain from solid-js/web or solid-js/store; no Context.Provider, onMount, createComputed, batch, splitProps or mergeProps remain.

title: Solid 2 test suite migration
description:
Migrate the existing suite to Solid 2 timing and add a contract suite for the new
semantics.

This is the largest and riskiest part of the migration, and the reason is not obvious
from reading the source. The current tests contain 8+ assertions of the form

  atom.set((prev) => prev + 1)
  expect(result()).toBe(1)

These pass today only because BOTH halves of the chain are synchronous:
@tanstack/store's atom.set notifies subscribers synchronously (propagate ->
shallowPropagate -> flush(), packages/store/src/atom.ts:249-261) into a Solid 1 signal
that also propagates synchronously. Under Solid 2 the second half defers to a
microtask, so every one of those reads returns the OLD value.

Types will not catch any of this. The regressions are all semantic, which is why the
contract suite matters as much as the migration itself.

Verified facts to build on:
- @solidjs/testing-library@1.0.0-beta.2 calls flush() internally only in renderHook
  (twice, at render time). A later .set() still needs an explicit settle.
- render() is fully synchronous; @solidjs/web's render flushes internally.
- fireEvent does NOT flush. Not used by this suite today, but relevant if added.
- Auto-cleanup needs a GLOBAL afterEach; this project has an explicit
  afterEach(cleanup) in tests/test-setup.ts. Keep it.
- flush() throws if called inside onSettled or createTrackedEffect.
- One awaited microtask settles everything, so await Promise.resolve() is a valid
  settle in async tests.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm --filter @tanstack/solid-store test:lib is green; the Solid 2 timing contract (deferred imperative reads, ownedWrite, unsubscribe-on-dispose) is pinned by explicit tests rather than left implicit.

title: Solid 2 toolchain flip
description:
Move every Solid dependency in the repo from Solid 1 to solid-js 2.0.0-beta.30 and
repoint the build/type toolchain at @solidjs/web.

This epic blocks all the others: nothing in the adapter source, tests or examples can
be verified until the workspace installs and typechecks against Solid 2. Land it as a
single coherent change so the tree is never half-migrated.

Decisions already taken:
- Solid 2 ONLY, on main. Breaking major of @tanstack/solid-store, no Solid 1 line,
  no dual-support shim.
- Pin 2.0.0-beta.30 (not the table repo's beta.29). Verified safe: @solidjs/signals
  type declarations are byte-identical between beta.29 and beta.30; the only runtime
  delta is a zombie-recompute cancellation fix in core/scheduler.js plus minifier
  symbol churn. queueMicrotask(flush) deferral is unchanged.
- Scope covers packages/solid-store, all 5 examples/solid/*, and packages/store's
  Solid benchmark, so exactly one solid-js version exists in the tree.

Reference: /home/kaalin/dev/table (branch beta, packages/solid-table) is a completed
migration of the same shape. Porting guide: ~/.claude/plans/solid-2-companion-porting-guide.md
acceptance_criteria: pnpm install completes with zero unmet peer warnings for solid-js, @solidjs/web, @solidjs/testing-library and vite-plugin-solid; a single solid-js version (2.0.0-beta.30) resolves across the workspace; pnpm test:sherif and pnpm test:knip are green.
close_reason: All six children closed: deps repointed at beta.30, peer relaxation landed via peerDependencyRules, jsxImportSource flipped, bench ported, ESLint rule added, install clean (sherif green, knip green, zero solid peer warnings, single solid-js@2.0.0-beta.30 in the tree).

title: Write the release changeset
description:
Create a changeset for @tanstack/solid-store. The body must tell an upgrading user
three things, in descending order of how likely they are to be bitten:

1. Imperative read-after-write is no longer synchronous. Reading a selector in the
   same synchronous tick as a store write returns the previous value. Reads from JSX,
   memos and effects are unaffected. Pass { settleOnRead: true } to useSelector to opt
   a specific selector back into read-your-writes, or await a microtask.

2. @solidjs/web is now a required peer dependency alongside solid-js.

3. Solid 1 is no longer supported. Peer range is >=2.0.0-beta.30 <3.0.0.

Also worth a line: createStoreContext's StoreProvider is unchanged from the consumer's
side - the Context.Provider -> Context change is internal.
design: minor, not major: the package is at 0.11.0, and under 0.x this repo treats minor as the breaking-change slot. Note .changeset/config.json sets onlyUpdatePeerDependentsWhenOutOfRange: true, and examples are in the ignore array as @tanstack/store-example-*, so their dep bumps need no changeset of their own.
acceptance_criteria: a changeset exists marking @tanstack/solid-store as a minor bump, whose body names all three breaking changes: Solid 2 only peer range, @solidjs/web as a new required peer, and non-synchronous imperative read-after-write.

title: Write the Solid 2 guide page for solid-store
description:
New file: docs/framework/solid/guide/solid-2.md

Must cover:

1. Upgrade steps - solid-js and @solidjs/web at 2.0.0-beta.30, vite-plugin-solid at
   3.0.0-next.21, tsconfig jsxImportSource: "@solidjs/web". Note that solid-js/web
   and solid-js/store no longer exist as subpaths.

2. The timing contract. This is the section that earns the page:
   - Reactive reads need nothing. JSX, memos and effect computes all re-run when the
     graph settles, so a selector read in a component is unaffected.
   - Imperative reads are stale for exactly the synchronous tick of the write:
        store.setState(1)
        selected()   // still the old value
     One awaited microtask settles everything - the write itself arms
     queueMicrotask(flush) - so `await Promise.resolve()` is a valid settle.
   - settleOnRead: true opts a selector into read-your-writes. Off by default because
     it costs a flush per untracked, unowned read.
   - The precise rule for when the settle happens: only when there is no tracking
     observer AND no owner. Component setup and anything re-entered through
     runWithOwner are owned scopes and see the committed value.
   - flush() from solid-js throws inside onSettled/createTrackedEffect and is a silent
     no-op inside an ordinary effect callback.

3. Why the adapter sets ownedWrite: true - @tanstack/store notifies synchronously from
   set(), and the callback inherits whatever scope the caller was in.

4. createStoreContext under Solid 2 - the context object is its own provider.

5. [STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED]: dev-build only, no production cost. It is benign when the
   surrounding JSX tracks the same value through another path, and a genuine staleness
   bug when a function reads a reactive value directly and returns a plain value.
   Because the diagnostic discriminates between those, a blanket untrack() would hide
   the only case worth catching. Fold in whatever D5 concludes.

Optional, if it comes up during the examples work: a note that a Solid store proxy
passed as store state never changes identity, so anything memoizing on identity will
not see updates.
design: Condense from table/docs/framework/solid/guide/solid-2.md rather than writing fresh - it is already a validated write-up of the same semantics. Cut everything table-specific (FlexRender, column defs, virtualization) and everything about APIs this package does not use (splitProps/omit, mergeProps/merge, onMount/onSettled, createComputed). What is left is small and that is correct: this package's whole Solid surface is a signal bridge and a context.
acceptance_criteria: docs/framework/solid/guide/solid-2.md exists and covers: the upgrade steps and dep pins, the removed-API table, the timing contract, settleOnRead, the ownedWrite rationale, context-as-provider, and [STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED] guidance.

title: Audit the simple example's prop-closing selector under Solid 2
description:
examples/solid/simple/src/index.tsx does:

  const count = useSelector(store, (state) => state[props.animals])

The selector closes over props.animals. useSelector is not reactive to selector
identity, so this only works because the prop never changes in this app - already true
under Solid 1.

What is new under Solid 2: the selector runs eagerly once during
`selector(source.get())` in the untracked component body, reading props.animals there.
Solid 2's dev build may emit:

  [STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED] Reactive value read directly in <Display> will not update.
  Move it into a tracking scope (JSX, a memo, or an effect's compute function).

Determine:
1. Does it actually fire? (run the example, check the console)
2. If it does, is it benign here - the JSX reads count() in a tracked scope, and
   props.animals is static - or does it point at a real staleness trap for users who
   copy this pattern with a prop that DOES change?
3. If it is a trap, what is the recommended shape instead, and does quick-start.md
   need to change with it?

Record the answer on this issue either way. It feeds the docs guide (epic E).
design: This matters out of proportion to its size because quick-start.md is essentially this example verbatim - it is the pattern users will copy. [STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED] is a discriminating diagnostic and should not be blanket-silenced with untrack(): it is benign when the surrounding JSX tracks the same value through another path, and a genuine staleness bug when a function reads a reactive value directly and returns a plain value. Decide which case this is rather than suppressing it.
acceptance_criteria: a verdict is recorded on whether useSelector(store, (state) => state[props.animals]) emits [STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED] under Solid 2's dev build, and whether the pattern should change; if it should, both the example and docs/framework/solid/quick-start.md are updated together.
notes:
VERDICT: the existing example and quick-start.md are correct as written. No change needed to either.

Probed under the real Solid 2 dev runtime (jsdom + vite-plugin-solid; the Chrome extension was not connected, and this is more reproducible anyway). Verified first that console.warn is the emission path -- @solidjs/signals' warnStrictReadUntracked() ends in console.warn(message) -- so a spy genuinely observes it.

Static prop (what the example actually does):
  useSelector(store, (state) => state[props.animals])  with  <Display animals="dogs" />
  => ZERO diagnostics, reactivity correct. A static JSX attribute compiles to a plain
  value rather than a getter, so no reactive value is read untracked and there is
  nothing to report.

Dynamic prop (the trap a reader could fall into):
  <Display animals={animals()} /> where animals is a useSelector accessor
  => value goes genuinely STALE (stuck at 7 after flipping to a key holding 41),
     and Solid 2 emits exactly one warning:
     '[STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED] Reactive value read directly in <Display> will not
      update. Move it into a tracking scope...'

So the diagnostic discriminates precisely: silent for the documented pattern, loud and
correctly-pointed for the broken one. This is not new behaviour -- useSelector has
always captured its selector once -- but Solid 2 is the first version that reports it.

Both cases are now pinned permanently in tests/selector-patterns.test.tsx rather than
left as a one-off probe. The dynamic case is concrete material for the docs guide
(store-yj0.1).

title: Confirm vitest needs no manual resolve conditions, by negative control
description:
packages/solid-store/vitest.config.ts already runs vite-plugin-solid via plugins:
[solid()], so it should need no changes at all for Solid 2 beyond the plugin version
bump in A1.

Verify rather than assume:
1. Run the suite as-is. Green.
2. Temporarily comment out solid() from plugins. Re-run. Expect failure - solid-js@2
   maps the bare node condition to dist/server.js, an inert server runtime where
   effects never run and nothing defers.
3. Restore the plugin. Record the observed failure mode on this issue.

If step 2 unexpectedly still passes, something else is supplying the conditions and
that needs understanding before shipping.

For contrast, the config that IS needed when there is no plugin (relevant to A4's
benchmark, which runs under packages/store's plugin-less vitest setup):

  resolve: { conditions: ['browser', 'development'] },
  ssr: { resolve: { conditions: ['browser', 'development'] } },
  test: { server: { deps: { inline: [/solid-js/] } } }
design: Worth an explicit issue because the porting guide flags manual resolve.conditions and server.deps.inline as a likely hazard, and the table repo's spike (table-rcv.4(e)) proved the opposite for a plugin-enabled config: vite-plugin-solid 3 injects [solid, development, browser, ...] itself in test mode. Recording the negative control here prevents a future reader from adding dead config 'just in case'.
acceptance_criteria: the suite runs green with packages/solid-store/vitest.config.ts unchanged apart from nothing; a temporary removal of the solid() plugin is shown to fail the suite with an inert runtime; the plugin is restored and the finding is recorded on this issue.
notes:
CONFIRMED, but the negative control is weaker here than in the table repo and the plan overstated what it would show.

vitest.config.ts needed NO resolve.conditions / server.deps.inline changes. It already runs vite-plugin-solid, and bumping that to 3.0.0-next.21 was sufficient. Suite: 36 passed.

Negative control (plugin removed): the suite does fail, but the first thing that breaks is the JSX transform, not module resolution -- 'Failed to parse source for import analysis because the content contains invalid JS syntax'. Both test files are .tsx. So this proves the plugin is load-bearing but does NOT isolate the browser/development conditions claim.

The conditions claim is instead proven positively, by evidence already collected:
  - the ownedWrite mutation run produced [REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE], which is a
    DEV-build diagnostic and does not exist in the inert server build
  - deferred-then-settle behaviour works at all, which requires the live client
    scheduler; the server build's flush() is a no-op and memos compute once

Conclusion: the conditions are correct and no manual vite config is warranted. Do not add resolve.conditions here 'just in case'.

Note for packages/store: its vitest config does NOT run vite-plugin-solid, so if anyone runs pnpm test:bench there, solid-js@2 will resolve to the inert server build and the Solid bench will measure nothing. Filed separately.

- useSelector returns Accessor<number> for writable AND readonly sources
- useAtom rejects readonly atoms (the @ts-expect-error at line 46 must still error)
- createStoreContext preserves keyed atom and store types

These run in vitest typecheck mode only (vitest's typecheck.include defaults to
**/*.test-d.?(c|m)[jt]s?(x)), so they are type-level assertions, not executed tests.
That matters: they call useSelector at the top level of a test() callback with no
owner, which at runtime would leak a subscription - see the no-owner issue in the
adapter epic.
acceptance_criteria: tests/test.test-d.ts covers UseSelectorOptions.settleOnRead; all existing expectTypeOf assertions still hold; pnpm --filter @tanstack/solid-store test:types passes on TS 5.6, 5.7, 5.8 and 6.0.

title: Decide behaviour for useSelector called with no owner
description:
useSelector registers onCleanup to unsubscribe. Called from a component body that is
the right thing. Called at module scope, or anywhere with no owner, onCleanup silently
does nothing and the @tanstack/store subscription is never torn down.

This is not new in Solid 2 - Solid 1 warned about it - but Solid 2 makes it quieter,
so it is worth an explicit decision now rather than a bug report later.

Options:
  (a) dev-only warn:
        if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production' && getOwner() === null) {
          console.warn('useSelector was called outside a reactive root. Its store ' +
            'subscription will never be disposed. Call it inside a component or ' +
            'wrap the call in createRoot.')
        }
  (b) document only, no runtime cost.

Note if (a) is chosen: it interacts with the settleOnRead guard, which also reads
getOwner(). Keep the two reads separate and clearly commented so a future reader does
not conflate them.
design: In Solid 2, runWithOwner(null, fn) means 'detach' rather than failing, and onCleanup outside an owner is a silent no-op - so an unowned useSelector never unsubscribes and leaks for the process lifetime. The table repo hit the same class of problem in createTable.ts and chose a dev-only console.warn ('createTable was called outside a reactive root. Table computations will never be disposed...'), specifically because the Solid 1 crash it replaced had become a silent leak. Weigh that against useSelector being a much smaller unit that users may reasonably call inside their own createRoot wrappers.
acceptance_criteria: a decision is recorded and implemented: either a dev-only console.warn when getOwner() is null at useSelector time, or an explicit documented statement that module-scope usage leaks its subscription; whichever is chosen is covered by a test or a doc line.
close_reason:
DECISION: document, do not warn.

Chose the documentation option over a dev-only console.warn for three reasons:
  1. No adapter in this repo uses process.env.NODE_ENV in src (verified by grep across
     packages/*/src). Adding it would introduce a node-ism and a new convention into a
     browser package that is otherwise free of both, and it lands in the shipped ESM.
  2. The behaviour is not new to Solid 2. onCleanup outside an owner was already a
     no-op under Solid 1, so this is not a migration regression.
  3. useSelector is a small enough unit that callers legitimately wrap it in their own
     createRoot, which supplies an owner - a warn would need to distinguish those and
     could not.

Landed as an @remarks block on useSelector's JSDoc (so it flows into the generated
reference docs) plus an Ownership section in the Solid 2 guide. Both state that an
unowned useSelector stays subscribed for the process lifetime, and the guide notes why
Solid 2 makes this quieter rather than louder: runWithOwner(null, fn) means detach
rather than fail.

title: Solid 2 examples migration
description:
Move the five examples/solid apps (atoms, simple, store-actions, store-context, stores)
to Solid 2.

They consume @tanstack/solid-store via workspace:* and pin solid-js ^1.9.12, so they
break the moment the adapter's peer range moves. They must migrate with it.

The good news: their Solid 1 surface is tiny. All five are structurally identical and
use exactly two Solid-1 things - `import { render } from 'solid-js/web'` and JSX with
jsxImportSource: solid-js. Confirmed absent across all five: onMount, createEffect,
createMemo, createSignal, splitProps, mergeProps, createStore from solid-js/store, and
every control-flow component (For/Show/Index/Switch/Match/Suspense/ErrorBoundary).
Props are read through the props object without destructuring, which is Solid-2-safe.

So D1-D3 are a mechanical three-line-per-example sweep. The real work is D4/D5, which
audit the two examples with patterns worth a second look under Solid 2's stricter dev
diagnostics.

Do NOT rename any example directory: scripts/verify-links.ts maps
/docs/framework/solid/examples/<name> to examples/solid/<name> and asserts the
directory exists, so a rename fails pnpm test:docs.
acceptance_criteria: all 5 examples/solid/* build and run against Solid 2; each is exercised in a browser and its reactivity confirmed; any [STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED] dev warnings are recorded with a verdict (benign or real).

title: packages/store Solid benchmark resolves the inert server runtime
description:
Discovered while confirming that packages/solid-store needs no manual vite resolve
conditions (store-7qc.5).

packages/store/vitest.config.ts does NOT run vite-plugin-solid - it has no Solid JSX,
so it never needed it. Under Solid 1 that was fine. Under Solid 2 it is not:
solid-js@2 maps the bare `node` condition to dist/server.js, an inert server runtime
where effects never run, flush() is a no-op and memos compute exactly once.

So tests/derived.bench.ts, ported in store-cd2.4, will now measure a signal write that
propagates to nothing - making Solid look artificially fast against Vue, Preact,
Angular and TanStack in the same suite.

Not caught by CI: `test:bench` is a separate script (vitest bench) and is not part of
test:ci or test:pr. The bench IS typechecked and linted, which is why the port was
needed at all.

Fix is one of:
  (a) add to packages/store/vitest.config.ts
        resolve: { conditions: ['browser', 'development'] },
        ssr: { resolve: { conditions: ['browser', 'development'] } },
        test: { server: { deps: { inline: [/solid-js/] } } }
      and verify the other benches (vue, preact, angular) still resolve correctly -
      setting resolve.conditions REPLACES Vite's defaults rather than appending, so
      this needs checking rather than assuming
  (b) add vite-plugin-solid to that package and let it inject the conditions
  (c) accept it and document the bench as not comparable for Solid

Verify by asserting inside the bench that the effect half actually ran.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm --filter @tanstack/store test:bench runs the Solid bench against the live client runtime, or the bench is explicitly documented/skipped as unrepresentative.
close_reason:
Fixed and pinned. Confirmed the diagnosis empirically first: a probe under packages/store's vitest config showed the effect half never ran ([] instead of [4]) and the memo computed exactly once - the signature of solid-js@2's inert server build.

Fix was option (a): resolve.conditions + ssr.resolve.conditions of ['browser','development'] plus server.deps.inline for solid-js and @solidjs/signals in packages/store/vitest.config.ts. Checked the concern that setting resolve.conditions REPLACES Vite's defaults rather than appending - the full packages/store suite (vue, preact, angular, and core) still passes: 34 passed, 1 skipped.

Impact was material, not cosmetic. The Solid bench went from 1,026,833 hz to 186,172 hz once it started measuring real propagation - a ~5.5x inflation that had it reading as the second-fastest library in the comparison, ahead of Preact and Vue. It now sits alongside TanStack, which is plausible.

Guarded by tests/solid-runtime.test.ts, which asserts the effect half runs and the memo recomputes. That test fails on the inert build, so the conditions cannot be dropped silently.

title: Guard the built dist against client-only @solidjs/web imports
description:
packages/solid-store/src/createStoreContext.tsx contains JSX, so the built dist WILL
import from @solidjs/web - specifically createComponent. That is SSR-safe.

Add a small script, wired ahead of publint in the package's test:build script, that
parses dist/**/*.js for @solidjs/web imports and fails on any specifier outside:

  new Set(['createComponent', 'memo'])

This keeps the package usable under SSR. It is P3 - do it if the migration is
otherwise settled, skip it if time is short and file the follow-up.
design: Simplify heavily from table/packages/solid-table/scripts/check-ssr-safe-dist.mjs (18.7KB, self-testing against fixtures). This package compiles exactly one JSX site - the <Context value> in createStoreContext.tsx - so the expected import surface is a single createComponent call. That makes an allow-list check cheap and the blast radius of a regression easy to see. Worth doing because @solidjs/web's server build replaces client-only exports with throwing stubs, so an accidental client-only import turns into a runtime crash at module scope under SSR rather than a build error.
acceptance_criteria: a check wired into test:build fails if dist/**/*.js imports any name from @solidjs/web outside an allow-list of createComponent and memo; the check passes on the current dist.
close_reason: Added packages/solid-store/scripts/check-ssr-safe-dist.mjs, wired ahead of publint in test:build. Allow-list {createComponent, memo}; current dist imports exactly createComponent from the one JSX site in createStoreContext.tsx. Also rejects namespace and side-effect imports. Mutation-tested: injecting render/template fails with exit 1 and names both. Full test:ci green with it in place.

title: Add braced-effect-half ESLint rule to solid-store
design: Insurance rather than a current need: the ported src/ contains no effects at all. Included because the failure it guards is catastrophic and silent - a non-function return from an effect half permanently halts the reactive system process-wide (REACTIVITY_HALTED), so nothing later in the app updates and there is no error pointing at the cause. Copy the rule verbatim from table/packages/solid-table/eslint.config.js. The package's current eslint.config.js is a bare passthrough of the root config; react-store, preact-store and svelte-store are precedent for package-level rule additions.
acceptance_criteria: packages/solid-store/eslint.config.js adds a no-restricted-syntax rule scoped to src/** that rejects an expression-bodied arrow as the second argument of createEffect or createRenderEffect; pnpm --filter @tanstack/solid-store test:eslint is green.

title: Remove dangling useSetValue and useStoreActions references from docs
description:
PRE-EXISTING, not caused by this migration. Filed here only because the migration is
already touching these files.

docs/config.json's "Store API Reference" section lists, for EVERY framework block
(react, vue, solid, svelte, preact, angular):

  framework/<fw>/reference/functions/useSetValue
  framework/<fw>/reference/functions/useStoreActions

Neither page exists on disk, and neither function is exported by any package in
packages/*/src. The only trace anywhere is a stale doc-comment mention in
packages/preact-store/src/useCreateStore.ts:25.

scripts/verify-links.ts only checks markdown links, not config.json entries, which is
why pnpm test:docs has never caught this.

Also: examples/solid/atoms/README.md claims the example demonstrates useSetValue,
which does not exist in solid-store.

Fix by deleting the dangling nav entries and correcting the README, or split into a
separate PR if it would muddy the migration diff.
acceptance_criteria: docs/config.json no longer lists reference pages that do not exist on disk for any framework; examples/solid/atoms/README.md no longer claims to demonstrate useSetValue.
